rv.q: Crystal prowls the stage in slacks and a loosened tie with ease and perfect timing.
It can't be said that Billy Crystal doesn't know his audience. They eat up his menu of Jews, jazz and baseball, wrapped in Catskills-inspired comedy and heartfelt Mom-and-Pop sentiment.

I won't flatter Billy Crystal by saying he hasn't aged a bit: He's a little older and slower than when he debuted this theatrical memoir on Broadway nine years ago. True, the 65-year-old looks amazingly young (how he avoids aging is one area not mined for humor).

You may not want to miss this chance to see a master entertainer ply his trade - not to mention the rare opportunity to relish real, live Catskills humor on Broadway. (Alan Zweibel, one of the original 'Saturday Night Live' writers, contributed additional material.)
The core pleasures of this warmly affectionate portrait of a New York childhood involve nostalgia and sentiment, the sex and violence of today’s Broadway.
At one point in the return engagement of 700 Sundays, Billy Crystal recalls the first comedian he ever saw: an old-school tummler, circa 1958, prowling the stage at Kutsher's 'like a panther.
Crystal and original director Des McAnuff sustain a knowing goofiness that makes it all go down smoothly.
In a laugh-out-loud - if quite long - revival of his 2004 one-man, autobiographical show 700 Sundays, you can practically hear his heart soaring

Seeing as few of these shows, if any, have surpassed Crystal's heartwarming and hilarious tour de force, it's a pleasure to have it return for a run before the "Les Miz" revival takes over the Imperial Theatre.
Crystal has turned the story of his own coming-of-age into such a relatable piece of theater that any one anecdote may start your waterworks flowing, even while you're doubled over in laughter.
To his great credit, he doesn't coast on his credentials. In '700 Sundays,' he delivers the full measure of his talent.
'700 Sundays' is an irresistible blend of Borscht Belt shtick and heartwarming schmaltz.
Crystal's warmth and wit make '700 Sundays' a touching tribute to his father and a celebration of family bonds that resonates long after the final bow.
700 Sundays is a memory piece that pretty much remains the warmhearted, moving and extremely funny night out that it was back in 2004.
